vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: gws-tasks
Version: 1.0.10

The skill bundle provides standard documentation and instructions for an AI agent to interact with Google Tasks via a CLI tool named 'gws'. The SKILL.md file outlines legitimate CRUD operations for task lists and tasks, including discovery commands like 'gws schema'. No evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or prompt injection was found.

llm.summary: The skill's declared behavior (wrapping the 'gws' CLI for Google Tasks) is plausible, but it hides authentication and security details in an external shared SKILL.md and does not declare required credentials — you should inspect that shared file and the gws CLI before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name and description match the instructions: the skill is an instruction-only wrapper around the 'gws' CLI for Google Tasks. Requiring the 'gws' binary is proportionate to the stated purpose and no unrelated binaries or env vars are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md delegates auth, global flags, and 'security rules' to ../gws-shared/SKILL.md (outside this file). It also suggests running 'gws generate-skills' if that file is missing. That external dependency controls authentication and possibly other behavior but is not included here, so the runtime instructions are incomplete and could cause the agent to create or use files/configuration you haven't reviewed.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files — the skill is instruction-only and will not write new code to disk. This is lower risk, but it relies on an existing 'gws' binary whose provenance you should verify.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials, yet practical use of Google Tasks through a CLI requires authentication (OAuth tokens or service credentials) which are not declared here. Authentication is implicitly delegated to the referenced ../gws-shared/SKILL.md or the system gws config; that missing linkage makes it unclear what secrets/configs the skill will access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request 'always: true', does not include install hooks, and does not modify other skills; it appears to run only when invoked. No persistence or elevated platform privileges are requested in the metadata.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill looks like a thin wrapper for the 'gws' CLI and is otherwise coherent, but it omits where authentication comes from. Before installing or enabling it: (1) locate and read ../gws-shared/SKILL.md referenced in the instructions — that file likely contains the auth method and any security rules; (2) verify the origin and integrity of the 'gws' binary on your system (where it came from, what config files/tokens it uses); (3) if the shared SKILL.md is missing and the agent runs 'gws generate-skills', inspect any files that command would create before allowing it to run; (4) prefer skills that explicitly declare required credentials or explain how tokens are stored/used; (5) if unsure, run the gws CLI manually in a controlled environment to confirm behavior before granting the skill access.
